advisories.finding: MEASURED_FALSIFICATION ships as {attempted: 0, bound: 0, free: 0, unclaimed: 0, ratePercent: 0.0} under a comment reading 'MEASURED 2026-08-11 by --falsification over the written bytes of the subject'. The instrument's own guard (falsification_record_state) grades the record UNMEASURED ('attempted is not positive') and every channel fails loud: --selftest appends the failure and exits 1 even over a clean base (observed: 57/57 caught, then SELFTEST-FAIL); --falsification prints FALSIFICATION-UNMEASURED and exits 1; --limits prints '*** NOT YET MEASURED ON THESE BYTES ***'.

The false statement lives only in a source comment; no output channel presents the placeholder as a measurement, so no reader can be deceived by RUNNING the instrument — only by reading the comment. Repair requires a successor instrument (section 7.8: a new checker is a new file), which IR-RC28-A03 independently requires anyway.

advisories.severity: HOSTILE-INPUT ROBUSTNESS; no false verdict reachable
advisories.finding: parse_json accepts Python's non-standard Infinity/NaN JSON tokens, and canonical() serialises with allow_nan=False. A mutated subject carrying an operation whose value is Infinity at the one float-typed position (from: 200.0 matches v26's $.partC_retentionBounds.vectors.rows[6].bounds.keepCount) passes every operation guard, and canonical(effective) at resolve_subject then raises an UNCAUGHT ValueError: measured EXIT 1, EMPTY STDOUT, traceback on stderr. That is byte-for-byte the predecessor-B1 signature this file's header says was repaired: a crash presented at the findings exit code, with the refusal neither scoped nor named, and even the RT28-SUBJECT-MOVED notice lost because the crash precedes the banner. resolve_subject is called in main() outside any try; the same call is correctly wrapped inside --selftest and --falsification.
advisories.consequence: Requires deliberately mutated subject bytes, and the exit direction (1) is not a false pass, so this does not block standing on the retained bytes. A successor should refuse non-finite floats at parse (parse_constant hook) or wrap the main-line resolve_subject in the same named-refusal discipline as the modes.

advisories.severity: LATENT; latched shut by the GATED pin on the declared review
advisories.finding: _blocking_tally selects the MINIMUM integer over every object member whose folded key matches 'blocking' AND a counting word. 'nonBlockingFindingsCount' matches the 'blocking' substring, so a document carrying {blockingFindingsCount: 4, nonBlockingFindingsCount: 0} tallies as 0 blockers (demonstrated in an in-memory probe). A rejecting review with zero non-blocking findings would satisfy the terminus test's 'reports ZERO blocking findings'.
advisories.consequence: Unreachable for this subject's verdict: the declared review retention-tiers.v26.review-independent.json is GATED at ffd8a80d... and genuinely reports 0 blockers, and mutating it refuses at exit 2 before any tally. The defect affects only the discovered-population count on this corpus, but any successor that reuses this tally inherits it. Anchor the regex on a word boundary (or require the key NOT to match 'non.?blocking') and take the tally from the matched review's own verdict object rather than a document-wide minimum.

advisories.severity: BANNER PRECISION; covered by the oracle union
advisories.finding: cross_check_demotion's demotion scan substitutes the resolved document's after-rows into the pinned v24 cells (verified live: a doctored changed cell with outcome PROCEED-EPHEMERAL or PROCEED-DURABLE/write-false fires RT28-XCHECK immediately). The banner prints the biconditional line under 'ASSERTED OVER THE RESOLVED VALUE, NOT THE DELTA BYTES', which overstates that one line's subject.
advisories.consequence: The gap is closed by the executed reference: the same doctored value drives RT26-A-INV-19 to fire by name ('changed cell 1 has null d9Axes and derivedClass TERMINATION, not NOT-A-TERMINATION') - demonstrated this review - so no reachable silent pass exists; freeze law 14's protection on the resolved table rests on the executed reference plus the demotion half of the cross-check, and the banner should attribute the biconditional to the pinned population it actually walks.

advisories.finding: Three banner phrases are string literals, not measurements: '0 of them naming an operation of this artifact' (the 0 is hardcoded in the f-string; the real count IS computed and gated elsewhere), 'all explained by an operation path', and 'all IDENTITY'. Each is backed by a gate that emits a finding when violated, so a false literal can only print alongside a contradicting finding and the exit code stays honest - but a reader of the banner line alone reads a literal as a result, the exact presentation class section 7.2.2 grades.
advisories.consequence: A successor should interpolate the computed values it already holds.

advisories.finding: RT28-SUBJECT-MOVED and RT28-TREE-MOVED are notices only; the exit matrix ignores them. A run over a mid-run-moved tree, or over subject bytes that differ from the dispatched digest but produce no finding (the disclosed E1-E12 free-prose surfaces), still exits 0 with 'PASS'. The TREE-MOVED notice itself says the correct response is to re-run rather than read the output, yet a machine consumer keying on the exit code takes a PASS.
advisories.consequence: Documented behaviour, deliberate for SUBJECT-MOVED (refusing would hide every other finding); the residual is that nothing distinguishes 'PASS over the dispatched bytes' from 'PASS over moved bytes' except prose. A successor could reserve a distinct exit for clean-run-over-moved-inputs.
